title: Precast T-beam: in-service flexure and construction stage
prompt:
A simply supported precast RC beam, 300 mm wide × 600 mm deep (effective depth $d = 540\ \mathrm{mm}$), spans 7.5 m between bearings. Beams are placed at 2.5 m centres and later receive a 100 mm cast-in-situ topping. Concrete C30/37, reinforcement B500B, normal-weight concrete $25\ \mathrm{kN/m^3}$.

In service (composite) the beam carries characteristic permanent load $g_k = 18\ \mathrm{kN/m}$ (including self-weight, topping and finishes) and imposed load $q_k = 12\ \mathrm{kN/m}$.

(a) Determine the ULS design moment using EC0 Eq. 6.10. [4]
(b) Design the tension reinforcement for the in-service condition, ignoring any flange contribution, and select bars. Check minimum steel. [8]
(c) During construction the precast beam alone must support its own weight, the wet topping and a construction load of $0.75\ \mathrm{kN/m^2}$ over the tributary width. Determine the construction-stage design moment and comment on whether the in-service reinforcement is adequate. [6]
(d) State two detailing requirements for the bottom bars at the bearings. [2]
approach: (a) $w_{\mathrm{Ed}} = 1.35 \times 18 + 1.5 \times 12 = 42.3\ \mathrm{kN/m}$ → $M_{\mathrm{Ed}} = w L^2/8 = 42.3 \times 7.5^2/8 = 297.4\ \mathrm{kNm}$.
(b) $K = M/(b d^2 f_{\mathrm{ck}}) = 297.4 \times 10^6/(300 \times 540^2 \times 30) = 0.113 < K' = 0.167$ (verify $K'$ against Singapore NA) → singly reinforced.

$A_s = M/(0.87 f_{\mathrm{yk}} z) = 1428\ \mathrm{mm^2}$ → provide 3H25 ($1473\ \mathrm{mm^2}$). $A_{\mathrm{s,min}} = 0.26 f_{\mathrm{ctm}}/f_{\mathrm{yk}} \cdot bd = 244\ \mathrm{mm^2}$ ($f_{\mathrm{ctm}} = 2.90\ \mathrm{N/mm^2}$) — OK. EC2 9.2.1.1.

(c) Beam $\mathrm{SW} = 0.3 \times 0.6 \times 25 = 4.5\ \mathrm{kN/m}$; wet topping = $2.5 \times 0.1 \times 25 = 6.25\ \mathrm{kN/m}$ → $g_k = 10.75\ \mathrm{kN/m}$; construction $q_k = 0.75 \times 2.5 = 1.875\ \mathrm{kN/m}$.

$w_{\mathrm{Ed}} = 1.35 \times 10.75 + 1.5 \times 1.875 = 17.3\ \mathrm{kN/m}$ → $M_{\mathrm{Ed}} = 121.8\ \mathrm{kNm}$; check the precast section ($b = 300$, $d = 540$) — the 3H25 is more than adequate, but check props/lifting points and top steel for hogging at lifting.
(d) EC2 9.2.1.4: at least 25% of span steel anchored at supports; anchorage beyond bearing face from $l_{\mathrm{bd}}$ with $\alpha$ factors; consider bearing nib/dowel detailing for precast.

title: Short braced column: axial, then axial + moment
prompt:
A braced short column, 400 mm × 400 mm, is cast in C35/45 concrete with B500 reinforcement. Cover to main bars gives $d_2 = 60\ \mathrm{mm}$ ($d_2/h = 0.15$).

(a) The column carries $N_{\mathrm{Ed}} = 3800\ \mathrm{kN}$ axially. Determine the area of longitudinal reinforcement required, stating the steel stress you adopt and why. [6]
(b) Determine the minimum design moment due to geometric imperfections, EC2 6.1(4). [3]
(c) The column is now also subject to a first-order design moment $M_{\mathrm{Ed}} = 120\ \mathrm{kNm}$ about one axis. Calculate $N/(b h f_{\mathrm{ck}})$ and $M/(b h^2 f_{\mathrm{ck}})$ and describe how you would use a column design chart to determine $A_s$. [7]
(d) Check the steel against EC2 9.5.2 limits and specify link size and spacing. [4]
approach: (a) Pure compression: strain limited to $\varepsilon_{c2} = 0.002$ → $\sigma_s = E_s \varepsilon_{c2} = 400\ \mathrm{N/mm^2}$ ($< f_{\mathrm{yd}} = 435$). $N_{\mathrm{Rd}} = 0.567 f_{\mathrm{ck}} (A_c - A_s) + 400 A_s$.

$0.567 \times 35 \times 160\,000 = 3175\ \mathrm{kN}$ → $A_s = (3800 - 3175) \times 10^3/(400 - 19.8) = 1644\ \mathrm{mm^2}$ (≈$1562\ \mathrm{mm^2}$ if displaced concrete ignored) → 4H25 ($1963\ \mathrm{mm^2}$).
(b) $e_0 = \max(h/30,\ 20\ \mathrm{mm}) = 20\ \mathrm{mm}$ → $M_{\mathrm{min}} = 3800 \times 0.020 = 76\ \mathrm{kNm}$.

(c) $M_{\mathrm{Ed}} = 120\ \mathrm{kNm} > 76\ \mathrm{kNm}$ governs. $N/(bhf_{\mathrm{ck}}) = 3.8 \times 10^6/(400 \times 400 \times 35) = 0.679$; $M/(bh^2f_{\mathrm{ck}}) = 120 \times 10^6/(400 \times 400^2 \times 35) = 0.054$.

Read the $d_2/h = 0.15$ symmetric-reinforcement chart → $A_s f_{\mathrm{yk}}/(b h f_{\mathrm{ck}})$, then $A_{\mathrm{s,tot}}$. Note chart assumptions ($\alpha_{\mathrm{cc}}$, rectangular block) — verify $\alpha_{\mathrm{cc}}$ against Singapore NA.

(d) $A_{\mathrm{s,min}} = \max(0.10 N_{\mathrm{Ed}}/f_{\mathrm{yd}},\ 0.002 A_c) = \max(874,\ 320)\ \mathrm{mm^2}$; $A_{\mathrm{s,max}} = 0.04 A_c = 6400\ \mathrm{mm^2}$. Links $\ge \max(6,\ \phi/4)$; spacing $\le \min(20\phi_{\min},\ b,\ 400\ \mathrm{mm})$ reduced by 0.6 near beams/slabs (9.5.3).

title: Unrestrained platform beam: LTB check and remedies
prompt:
A steel platform beam spans 8.0 m between simple supports that provide torsional and lateral restraint at the ends only. The beam is a UKB 457×191×67 in S355 with: $h = 453.4\ \mathrm{mm}$, $b = 189.9\ \mathrm{mm}$, $t_w = 8.5\ \mathrm{mm}$, $t_f = 12.7\ \mathrm{mm}$, $r = 10.2\ \mathrm{mm}$, $A = 8550\ \mathrm{mm^2}$, $W_{\mathrm{pl,y}} = 1471 \times 10^3\ \mathrm{mm^3}$, $I_z = 1452 \times 10^4\ \mathrm{mm^4}$, $I_t = 37.1 \times 10^4\ \mathrm{mm^4}$, $I_w = 0.705 \times 10^{12}\ \mathrm{mm^6}$. Section is Class 1 in bending. $E = 210\,000$, $G = 81\,000\ \mathrm{N/mm^2}$.

Loading (UDL, applied at the shear centre): $g_k = 12\ \mathrm{kN/m}$ (incl. self-weight), $q_k = 10\ \mathrm{kN/m}$.

(a) Sketch the SFD and BMD with ULS values (EC0 6.10). [4]
(b) Check cross-section bending and shear resistance. [5]
(c) Calculate $M_{\mathrm{cr}}$ ($C_1 = 1.127$) and the LTB resistance $M_{\mathrm{b,Rd}}$ using EC3 6.3.2.3 for rolled sections. [8]
(d) The beam fails the LTB check. Propose two remedies and quantify one. [3]
approach: (a) $w_{\mathrm{Ed}} = 1.35 \times 12 + 1.5 \times 10 = 31.2\ \mathrm{kN/m}$ → $V_{\mathrm{Ed}} = 124.8\ \mathrm{kN}$ at supports, $M_{\mathrm{Ed}} = 31.2 \times 8^2/8 = 249.6\ \mathrm{kNm}$ at midspan (parabolic BMD).

(b) $t_f = 12.7 \le 16$ → $f_y = 355$. $M_{\mathrm{c,Rd}} = W_{\mathrm{pl}} f_y/\gamma_{\mathrm{M0}} = 522.2\ \mathrm{kNm} \ge 249.6$ OK. $A_v = A - 2bt_f + (t_w + 2r)t_f = 4094\ \mathrm{mm^2}$ → $V_{\mathrm{pl,Rd}} = A_v f_y/\sqrt{3} = 839\ \mathrm{kN}$ OK; $V_{\mathrm{Ed}} < 0.5V_{\mathrm{pl,Rd}}$ so no M–V interaction.
(c) $M_{\mathrm{cr}} = C_1\pi^2EI_z/L^2 \sqrt{I_w/I_z + L^2GI_t/(\pi^2EI_z)} = 177.7\ \mathrm{kNm}$.

$\bar{\lambda}_{\mathrm{LT}} = \sqrt{W_{\mathrm{pl}} f_y/M_{\mathrm{cr}}} = 1.714$; $h/b = 2.39 > 2$ → curve c, $\alpha_{\mathrm{LT}} = 0.49$; $\bar{\lambda}_{\mathrm{LT,0}} = 0.4$, $\beta = 0.75$ (NA choice — verify Singapore NA).

(d) Remedies: intermediate lateral restraint (bracing/floor connection to compression flange), a heavier/wider section, or a closed/hollow section. With a midspan restraint ($L = 4.0\ \mathrm{m}$, conservatively $C_1 = 1.0$): $M_{\mathrm{cr}} = 477.8\ \mathrm{kNm}$, $\bar{\lambda}_{\mathrm{LT}} = 1.045$, $\chi_{\mathrm{LT}} = 0.612$, $M_{\mathrm{b,Rd}} = 319.5\ \mathrm{kNm} \ge 249.6$ OK.

title: Pinned column buckling and bolted splice
prompt:
A UKC 254×254×73 in S355 is used as a pin-ended column of system length 5.0 m about both axes. $A = 9310\ \mathrm{mm^2}$, $i_y = 110\ \mathrm{mm}$, $i_z = 64.6\ \mathrm{mm}$, $t_f = 14.2\ \mathrm{mm}$, $h/b = 0.98$. Section is Class 1 under compression.

(a) Determine the flexural buckling resistance $N_{\mathrm{b,Rd}}$ about both axes and state which governs. [10]
(b) The column is spliced with M20 class 8.8 bolts in single shear, threads in the shear plane ($A_s = 245\ \mathrm{mm^2}$). Determine the shear resistance per bolt (EC3-1-8 Table 3.4) and the number of bolts if the splice must transfer 25% of $N_{\mathrm{b,Rd}}$. [6]
(c) Briefly explain how the check changes if the column also carries end moments. [4]
approach: (a) $\varepsilon = \sqrt{235/355} = 0.814$; $\lambda_1 = 93.9\varepsilon = 76.4$.

(b) $F_{\mathrm{v,Rd}} = \alpha_v f_{\mathrm{ub}} A_s/\gamma_{\mathrm{M2}} = 0.6 \times 800 \times 245/1.25 = 94.1\ \mathrm{kN}$ ($\gamma_{\mathrm{M2}}$ — verify Singapore NA). $0.25 \times 1760 = 440\ \mathrm{kN}$ → $n = 440/94.1 = 4.7$ → 6 bolts (symmetrical). Also check bearing $F_{\mathrm{b,Rd}}$.
(c) Combined: EC3 6.3.3 Eqs 6.61/6.62 with interaction factors $k_{yy}$, $k_{zy}$ (Annex A or B); check cross-section 6.2.9 and LTB $\chi_{\mathrm{LT}}$ for $M_y$.

title: Strip footing on sand: EC7 DA1 and Schmertmann settlement
prompt:
A 2.0 m wide strip footing is founded at 1.0 m depth in a medium-dense sand ($\gamma = 19\ \mathrm{kN/m^3}$, $c' = 0$, $\phi'_k = 32^\circ$). The water table is well below the zone of influence. The footing carries a central vertical line load $G_k = 250\ \mathrm{kN/m}$ and $Q_k = 100\ \mathrm{kN/m}$ (both including footing self-weight and backfill).

CPT results below founding level: 0–2 m $q_c = 6\ \mathrm{MPa}$; 2–4 m $q_c = 8\ \mathrm{MPa}$; 4–6 m $q_c = 10\ \mathrm{MPa}$; 6–8 m $q_c = 12\ \mathrm{MPa}$.

(a) Verify bearing resistance to EC7 Design Approach 1, Combinations 1 and 2, using Annex D. [10]
(b) Estimate the settlement under characteristic (SLS) loads using Schmertmann's method with $E = 3.5 q_c$ (strip), ignoring creep ($C_2 = 1$). [8]
(c) Comment on which limit state governs the design. [2]
approach: $R/A' = q'N_q + 0.5\gamma B'N_{\gamma} = 19 \times 23.18 + 0.5 \times 19 \times 2 \times 27.72 = 967\ \mathrm{kPa}$ → $R_d = 1934\ \mathrm{kN/m} \ge 487.5$ ✓.

DA1-C2 (A2+M2+R1): $V_d = 1.0 \times 250 + 1.3 \times 100 = 380\ \mathrm{kN/m}$; $\phi'_d = \arctan(\tan 32^\circ/1.25) = 26.56^\circ$ → $N_q = 12.59$, $N_{\gamma} = 11.59$ → $R_d = 919\ \mathrm{kN/m} \ge 380$ ✓ (C2 is critical in utilisation, 41%).
(b) $\Delta p = (250 + 100)/2 - 19 \times 1 = 156\ \mathrm{kPa}$; $\sigma'_{v0} = 19\ \mathrm{kPa}$; $\sigma'_{\mathrm{vp}}$ at $z = B = 2\ \mathrm{m}$ below base (3 m depth) = 57 kPa.
$s = C_1C_2\Delta p \sum(I_z/E)\Delta z = 0.939 \times 156 \times 1.051 \times 10^{-4} \approx 15.4\ \mathrm{mm}$.
(c) ULS has large reserve; settlement (≈15 mm, acceptable vs typical 25 mm limit) is the more relevant criterion — confirm with structure's tolerance to differential settlement.

title: Cantilever retaining wall: earth pressure and sliding (DA1)
prompt:
A cast-in-situ RC cantilever retaining wall retains 5.0 m of dry granular backfill ($\gamma = 18\ \mathrm{kN/m^3}$, $c' = 0$, $\phi'_k = 30^\circ$) with a horizontal ground surface carrying a variable surcharge $q_k = 10\ \mathrm{kPa}$. The wall base is 3.5 m wide and the total characteristic vertical load on the base (wall + soil over heel) is $W_k = 220\ \mathrm{kN/m}$. Base friction $\delta = \phi'$ (cast against soil). Ignore passive resistance in front of the toe. Use Rankine pressures on a vertical virtual back.

(a) Calculate the design horizontal thrust for DA1-C1 and DA1-C2. [8]
(b) Verify sliding for both combinations. [6]
(c) If sliding is not satisfied, propose two practical measures. [3]
(d) Sketch the pressure distribution with values. [3]
approach: (a) C1: $\phi'_d = 30^\circ$, $K_a = 1/3$. $H_{\mathrm{soil}} = 1.35 \times 0.5 \times K_a \gamma H^2 = 1.35 \times 75 = 101.3\ \mathrm{kN/m}$; $H_q = 1.5 \times K_a q H = 1.5 \times 16.7 = 25.0\ \mathrm{kN/m}$ → $H_d = 126.3\ \mathrm{kN/m}$.

C2: $\phi'_d = \arctan(\tan 30^\circ/1.25) = 24.79^\circ$, $K_a = 0.409$. $H_{\mathrm{soil}} = 1.0 \times 0.5 \times 0.409 \times 18 \times 25 = 92.1$; $H_q = 1.3 \times 0.409 \times 10 \times 5 = 26.6$ → $H_d = 118.6\ \mathrm{kN/m}$.
(b) Sliding $R_d = V_d \tan\delta_d$ with favourable W at $\gamma_G = 1.0$: C1 $R_d = 220 \tan 30^\circ = 127.0 \ge 126.3$ ✓ (marginal); C2 $R_d = 220 \tan 24.79^\circ = 101.6 < 118.6$ ✗ FAIL.
(c) Add a shear key below the base (mobilises passive resistance), widen the heel to increase W, or use a sloping base.
(d) Triangular soil pressure 0 → $K_a\gamma H$ (C2 char.: 36.8 kPa at base) plus rectangular $K_a q$ block (4.1 kPa).

title: Expressway incident shockwave and stopping sight distance
prompt:
An expressway lane group follows Greenshields' model with free-flow speed $v_f = 100\ \mathrm{km/h}$ and jam density $k_j = 120\ \mathrm{veh/km}$ (per lane).

(a) Determine capacity, critical density and speed at capacity. [3]
(b) Upstream traffic flows at 1800 veh/h/lane (uncongested). A lane-blocking incident causes a queue that discharges at 1200 veh/h/lane in the congested regime. Find the densities of both states and the speed and direction of the resulting shockwave. [8]
(c) Using AASHTO, determine the stopping sight distance for a design speed of 100 km/h ($t = 2.5\ \mathrm{s}$, $a = 3.4\ \mathrm{m/s^2}$) on (i) a level road and (ii) a 3% downgrade. [7]
(d) State one traffic-management measure to reduce secondary crashes at the queue tail. [2]
approach: (a) $q_{\mathrm{max}} = v_f k_j/4 = 3000\ \mathrm{veh/h}$; $k_c = k_j/2 = 60\ \mathrm{veh/km}$; $v_c = v_f/2 = 50\ \mathrm{km/h}$.
(b) $k = (k_j/2)[1 \mp \sqrt{1 - 4q/(v_f k_j)}]$. State A (uncongested, 1800): $k_A = 22.1\ \mathrm{veh/km}$. State B (congested, 1200): $k_B = 106.5\ \mathrm{veh/km}$.
$u_w = (q_B - q_A)/(k_B - k_A) = (1200 - 1800)/(106.5 - 22.1) = -7.1\ \mathrm{km/h}$ → backward-forming shockwave moving upstream at 7.1 km/h.
(c)(i) $\mathrm{SSD} = 0.278Vt + 0.039V^2/a = 69.5 + 114.7 = 184.2\ \mathrm{m}$ (AASHTO Green Book).
(d) Queue-tail warning via VMS / advance warning signs, variable speed limits, or traffic-incident management to clear quickly.

title: Trapezoidal canal: normal depth, critical depth and profile
prompt:
A long concrete-lined trapezoidal drainage canal has bottom width $b = 3.0\ \mathrm{m}$, side slopes 2H:1V, Manning $n = 0.015$ and bed slope $S_0 = 0.0008$. Design discharge $Q = 12\ \mathrm{m^3/s}$.

(a) Determine the normal depth $y_n$ and the mean velocity at normal depth. [7]
(b) Determine the critical depth $y_c$ and the Froude number at normal depth. [6]
(c) Classify the channel slope. A downstream weir raises the water depth to 2.2 m. Name and sketch the resulting water-surface profile. [5]
(d) State one PUB Code of Practice on Surface Water Drainage consideration for such an open drain. [2]
approach: (b) Critical: $Q^2T/(gA^3) = 1$ with $T = b + 2zy$ → $y_c = 0.947\ \mathrm{m}$. Fr at normal depth = $V/\sqrt{gD}$, $D = A/T = 0.885\ \mathrm{m}$ → $\mathrm{Fr} = 0.56$ (subcritical).
(c) $y_n > y_c$ → mild slope. Weir depth $2.2\ \mathrm{m} > y_n > y_c$ → M1 backwater curve, asymptotic to $y_n$ upstream and rising towards the weir.
(d) e.g. freeboard requirement, minimum self-cleansing velocity, maintenance access — check current PUB COP.

title: Primary clarifier and activated sludge sizing
prompt:
A water reclamation plant treats an average flow of $20\,000\ \mathrm{m^3/d}$.

(a) Size circular primary clarifiers for a surface overflow rate of $40\ \mathrm{m^3/(m^2\cdot d)}$ and a hydraulic detention time of 2.0 h, using a single tank: determine the area, diameter and side-water depth. [6]
(b) The primary effluent $\mathrm{BOD_5}$ is 180 mg/L. Determine the aeration tank volume for an F/M ratio of $0.30\ \mathrm{d^{-1}}$ with MLVSS = 2500 mg/L, and the hydraulic retention time. [6]
(c) Waste activated sludge is withdrawn from the return line at $150\ \mathrm{m^3/d}$ with a VSS of 8000 mg/L. Neglecting effluent solids, calculate the solids retention time (SRT). [4]
(d) Explain the effect on effluent quality and sludge settleability of operating at a much lower SRT. [4]
approach: (a) $A = Q/\mathrm{OR} = 20\,000/40 = 500\ \mathrm{m^2}$ → $D = \sqrt{4A/\pi} = 25.2\ \mathrm{m}$; $V = Q \cdot t = 20\,000 \times 2/24 = 1667\ \mathrm{m^3}$ → depth = 3.33 m. Check weir loading and peak-flow overflow rate.
(c) $\theta_c = VX/(Q_w X_r) = 4800 \times 2500/(150 \times 8000) = 10.0\ \mathrm{d}$.
(d) Low SRT → higher F/M, dispersed growth / poor flocculation, poorer settleability, little or no nitrification, higher effluent BOD/SS.

title: Reservoir-to-reservoir pipeline in series; upgrade with a parallel pipe
prompt:
Reservoir A (water level 100.0 m) supplies reservoir B (70.0 m) through two pipes in series: pipe 1, 800 m long, 400 mm diameter; pipe 2, 600 m long, 300 mm diameter. Take Darcy $f = 0.02$ for both. Minor loss coefficients: entrance 0.5 (on $v_1$), sudden contraction 0.3 (on $v_2$), exit 1.0 (on $v_2$).

(a) Determine the discharge. [8]
(b) Determine the hydraulic grade line elevation at the end of pipe 1 and sketch the EGL and HGL. [5]
(c) Pipe 2 is duplicated by an identical parallel 300 mm pipe (each with the same contraction and exit losses). Determine the new discharge. [5]
(d) Why might Hazen–Williams be preferred for a water-supply network check? [2]
approach: EGL at the end of pipe 1 = $100 - (v_1^2/2g)(0.5 + 40) = 92.90\ \mathrm{m}$; $\mathrm{HGL} = \mathrm{EGL} - v_1^2/2g = 92.72\ \mathrm{m}$. EGL drops in steps at each minor loss, with steeper slope in pipe 2.
Parallel pipes share the head and each carries Q/2: $30 = (v_1^2/2g)(40.5) + ((Q/2A_2)^2/2g)(41.3)$ → $Q = 0.357\ \mathrm{m^3/s}$ (+53 %).
Hazen–Williams is explicit in Q, C tables by material and age (notes p. 106); good for water at normal temperatures, not for other fluids or laminar flow.

title: Broad-crested weir, jump at the toe, V-notch for low flows
prompt:
A broad-crested weir spans a 4.0 m wide rectangular channel. The upstream head over the crest is 0.80 m (approach velocity negligible, free discharge, $C_d = 0.88$).

(a) Calculate the discharge and the critical depth on the crest. [6]
(b) At the toe of the weir the flow depth is 0.25 m. Show that a hydraulic jump can form, and calculate the sequent depth and the head loss. [8]
(c) For dry-weather flows a 90° V-notch ($C_d = 0.59$) is installed. Calculate the flow at a head of 0.30 m. [4]
(d) State one condition under which the weir becomes drowned and its rating no longer applies. [2]
approach: $Q = C_d(2/3)^{3/2}\sqrt{g} \cdot B \cdot h^{3/2} = 0.88 \times 0.544 \times 3.13 \times 4 \times 0.8^{1.5} = 4.29\ \mathrm{m^3/s}$; $q = 1.07\ \mathrm{m^2/s}$ → $y_c = (q^2/g)^{1/3} = 0.49\ \mathrm{m}$ (= 2/3 of the head on the crest).

Toe: $v_1 = q/0.25 = 4.29\ \mathrm{m/s}$, $\mathrm{Fr}_1 = 2.74 > 1$ (supercritical) → $y_2 = (y_1/2)(\sqrt{1 + 8\mathrm{Fr}_1^2} - 1) = 0.85\ \mathrm{m}$; $\Delta E = (y_2 - y_1)^3/(4y_1y_2) = 0.26\ \mathrm{m}$.
V-notch: $Q = C_d(8/15)\sqrt{2g} \cdot \tan 45^\circ \cdot h^{5/2} = 0.59 \times 0.533 \times 4.43 \times 0.3^{2.5} = 0.069\ \mathrm{m^3/s}$.
Drowning when the tailwater rises above about the critical-depth level on the crest (modular limit) — the downstream level then controls.

title: Unit hydrograph convolution, Gumbel design flood, Muskingum coefficients
prompt:
The 3-hour unit hydrograph (1 cm of excess rain) of a catchment has ordinates at 3-hour intervals: 0, 25, 60, 45, 30, 15, 5, $0\ \mathrm{m^3/s}$.

(a) Determine the catchment area. [3]
(b) A storm produces 2 cm then 3 cm of excess rainfall in two successive 3-hour periods. Determine the direct-runoff hydrograph and its peak. [7]
(c) Annual maximum floods have mean $420\ \mathrm{m^3/s}$ and standard deviation $130\ \mathrm{m^3/s}$ (long record). Estimate the 50-year flood by Gumbel and the risk that it is exceeded at least once in 25 years. [6]
(d) For routing through a downstream reach, $K = 12\ \mathrm{h}$ and $X = 0.2$ with $\Delta t = 6\ \mathrm{h}$. Calculate the Muskingum coefficients and check their sum. [4]
approach: Area = $\sum U \cdot \Delta t/1\ \mathrm{cm} = 180 \times 3 \times 3600/0.01 = 1.944 \times 10^8\ \mathrm{m^2} = 194\ \mathrm{km^2}$.
$\mathrm{DRH}_n = \sum P_m U_{n-m+1}$: 0, 50, 195, 270, 195, 120, 55, 15, $0\ \mathrm{m^3/s}$ → peak $270\ \mathrm{m^3/s}$ at 9 h (add base flow if required).
